findings.location: p.3, final sentence of the first paragraph
findings.claim: The stated positive n-dimensional image measure contradicts the Lusin N property in the same paragraph.
findings.proof: For 0<alpha<=n, H^alpha(E)=0 implies L^n(E)=0: restrict to bounded pieces and use diam(U)^n<=delta^(n-alpha)diam(U)^alpha for sufficiently fine covers. The stated Lusin N property then forces H^n(u(E))=0 in target R^n. Already n=m=1 is a direct obstruction: V^1L^{1,1}_loc is locally absolutely continuous, so every Lebesgue-null set has image of length zero. Full image Hausdorff dimension n does not imply positive H^n measure.
findings.impact: Introductory overstatement; no counterexample to a main Orlicz-Sobolev distortion theorem.
findings.repair: Retain only the supported full-dimension statement, with zero n-dimensional measure allowed; remove the positive-measure inference.
findings.counterevidence: Dimension n and zero H^n measure are compatible, and the main theorems impose the correct zero-measure conclusions.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: For 0<alpha<n, sufficiently fine diameter covers show H^alpha(E)=0 implies Lebesgue-n measure zero; alpha=n follows from proportionality. The N property in the same introductory discussion then prevents positive H^n image measure. Independently, n=m=1 gives locally absolutely continuous maps and the same obstruction. Full Hausdorff dimension does not imply positive top-dimensional measure.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The supported full-dimension assertion can survive; the false positivity inference is introductory and is not used as a main distortion theorem hypothesis.
independent_verification.repair_check: Delete the positivity assertion while retaining the appropriately supported dimension statement.

findings.location: p.5 equation(2.6), p.10 Remark3.2; related exact power normalization p.13 equation(3.24)
findings.claim: Two exact equalities/inequalities omit multiplicative normalization.
findings.proof: For n=1 and phi(r)=2r, H^phi=2L^1 differs literally from L^1, yet phi(r)/r=2 does not tend to infinity. Thus the equivalence preceding(2.6) requires non-equivalence up to constants rather than literal inequality. For phi(s)=s^n, J(s)=sB^{-1}(1) and psi(r)=r^n/[B^{-1}(1)]^n. With n=1,A(t)=4t^2, B=A and psi(r)=2r, not r. More generally for n>=2,A=t^p, B=c_B t^p where c_B=(n'-p')^(p-1), giving psi(r)=c_B^(alpha/(p+alpha-n))r^(alpha p/(p+alpha-n)).
findings.impact: Normalization of displayed examples; the measure-equivalence, distortion exponent and Lusin N deductions remain valid.
findings.repair: Use the displayed exact constants or explicitly state multiplicative equivalence. Theorem3.4's actual limit condition(2.6) remains the correct substantive hypothesis.
findings.counterevidence: Multiplication of a gauge by a positive constant does not change zero sets or finiteness of its Hausdorff measure.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: For n=1, phi(r)=2r gives H^phi=2 Lebesgue measure, not literal equality, while phi(r)/r=2 does not diverge. For phi(s)=s^n the definitions give J(s)=s B^{-1}(1), hence psi(r)=r^n/[B^{-1}(1)]^n, with an exact normalization constant.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Equivalence up to fixed positive factors preserves null sets, finiteness and the distortion exponent; the divergent-limit hypothesis of Theorem 3.4 is unaffected.
independent_verification.repair_check: Distinguish equality from comparability and either keep the constant or impose the stated normalization.

findings.claim: The explicit constant does not cover the allowed one-dimensional case.
findings.proof: Take n=m=1,p=2,alpha=1,u(x)=min(max(x,0),1),E=[0,1]. The map belongs to the homogeneous V^{1,2}(R,R), ||u'||_2=1 and H^1_infinity(E)=H^1_infinity(u(E))=1. With n'=infinity, the factor ((p-1)/(n'-p'))^(alpha(p-1)/(alpha+p-n)) is zero, so(3.16) gives 1<=0. Without that convention it is undefined at n=1. For the repair let tau=alpha p/(p+alpha-1). On an interval I, diam u(I)<=|I|^(1-1/p)(integral_I|u'|^p)^(1/p). Replace covering sets by their convex intervals and merge overlapping intervals; for alpha<=1 the alpha-cost cannot increase. The intervals have disjoint interiors. Holder's inequality for their sum yields sum diam u(I)^tau <= ||u'||_p^tau (sum|I|^alpha)^((p-1)/(p+alpha-1)). Infimizing proves the one-dimensional replacement with constant1.
findings.impact: False quantitative example at n=1; the general theorem uses B=A there and is not refuted.
findings.repair: Restrict the n'-p' formula to n>=2 and state the one-dimensional Holder estimate separately.
findings.counterevidence: The corrected one-dimensional estimate is attained by the clamp example for alpha=1 and agrees with the theorem's qualitative conclusions.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The admissible n=m=1, p=2, alpha=1 clamp u=min(max(x,0),1), E=[0,1] has derivative L2 norm one and both contents one. The n'-p' formula vanishes under n'=infinity and otherwise is undefined, giving a false specialized constant.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Theorem 3.5 uses B=A in dimension one and remains available. Interval convexification, merging and Holder yield tau=alpha*p/(p+alpha-1) and the stated correct one-dimensional content estimate.
independent_verification.repair_check: Restrict the defective specialization to n>=2 and use the independently checked one-dimensional interval estimate.

findings.location: p.19 Lemma4.3, equation(4.20) and the following monotonicity argument; correct input p.17 equation(4.6)
findings.claim: The denominator lacks its n-th power; the cited monotonicity is correspondingly insufficient as written.
findings.proof: Set v=phi(s)/s^n. The identity is phi(s)/J(s)^n = v/[B^{-1}(v)]^n. Exact test: n=2,A(t)=(27/8)t^4 gives B(t)=t^4 under(2.27); phi(s)=s, s=16 gives J=8 and actual left side1/4, while the printed right side is(1/16)/(1/2)=1/8. For A=a t^p, conjugating explicitly gives B=a(n'-p')^(p-1)t^p, verifying the chosen normalization. To repair the proof, v/[B^{-1}(v)]^n=B(z)/z^n is nondecreasing by(4.6), with z=B^{-1}(v). Since v(s) is nonincreasing, their composition is nonincreasing. This proves exactly the claimed property(4.17), including n=1 by convexity.
findings.impact: The false equality and insufficient monotonicity proof establish Lemma4.3, explicitly used in Theorem3.1 p23(5.6), (5.9) and (5.13), and in Lemma4.10. Major for an invalid derivation in the main distortion machinery. Correcting it preserves the conclusions.
findings.repair: Restore the exponent n and use B(z)/z^n monotonicity, not merely the Young-function property B(z)/z.
findings.counterevidence: The already established (4.6) supplies the replacement B(z)/z^n argument; it is not a separately printed proof of(4.17)/(4.18). The source's actual proof uses false(4.20) and the different v/B^-1(v). Neither the gauge lemma nor Theorem3.1 is refuted.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The identity must be phi(s)/J(s)^n=v/[B^{-1}(v)]^n, v=phi(s)/s^n. For n=2, A(t)=27t^4/8, B(t)=t^4, phi(s)=s, s=16, the left side is 1/4 and the printed right side 1/8. The repaired monotonicity needs B(z)/z^n, furnished by (4.6), rather than merely B(z)/z.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The stronger premise (4.6) is available and supplies an explicit replacement proof. It is not a second valid printed proof of (4.17). Theorem 3.1 actually invokes Lemma 4.3 in (5.6), leading to (5.9) and (5.13); Lemma 4.10 also uses it.
independent_verification.repair_check: Restore the nth power and invoke (4.6) with the monotonicity of phi(s)/s^n. This repairs the claim but does not lower the severity of an invalid derivation used in the central distortion estimate. No counterexample to the corrected theorem is asserted.

findings.location: p.14 Example3.9, first branch of equation(3.28), alpha=0
findings.claim: The exponential inverse is not determined up to multiplicative constants by the stated slowly varying comparability.
findings.proof: Choose n=1,A(t)=t log(1+t),q=1,beta=-1. A''=(t+2)/(t+1)^2>0, and A(t)/t tends to0 at0 and infinity at infinity. For L=log(1/s)>=16 set phi(s)=s A(4/(sL^2))=4L^{-2}log(1+4e^L/L^2), and for s>=exp(-16) extend linearly with phi(s)/s constant. This is a continuous increasing gauge, phi/s is nonincreasing, and phi(s)~4/log(1/s). To check monotonicity, write z=4e^L/L^2. The derivative in L is 4L^{-3}[-2log(1+z)+(L-2)z/(1+z)], which is negative because its bracket is less than -L+4log L-2log4-2<0 for L>=16. Since B=A, exactly J(s)=4/L^2 and J^{-1}(r)=exp(-2/sqrt(r)). The printed comparison is exp(-1/sqrt(r)); their ratio tends to0. Nevertheless psi(r)=r log(1+r exp(2/sqrt(r)))~2sqrt(r), agreeing with(3.26). In general replace(3.28)'s alpha0 line by log(1/J^{-1}(r)) comparable to r^{-n/(q-n+1-beta)}, or retain constants inside exponential bounds. Compose with phi to obtain the correct final power.
findings.impact: False intermediate inverse comparison; the final critical gauge exponent survives the explicit calculation and corrected logarithmic argument.
findings.repair: Use logarithmic comparability/two exponential bounds. Also read the displayed J(s) asymptotics on pp.14-15 near zero, not the printed near-infinity label.
findings.counterevidence: The construction gives precisely the final power predicted by(3.26), so it is not a counterexample to that final gauge or Theorem3.1.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: With n=1, A(t)=t log(1+t) and phi(s)=s A(4/[s log(1/s)^2]) near zero, the Young-function and increasing-gauge hypotheses hold, phi(s)/s is nonincreasing, and B=A. Exactly J(s)=4/log(1/s)^2, so J^{-1}(r)=exp(-2/sqrt(r)); its ratio to exp(-1/sqrt(r)) tends to zero. Multiplicative comparability is false.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Composition gives psi(r)=r log(1+r exp(2/sqrt(r)))~2 sqrt(r), preserving the final gauge exponent. The source's final conclusion is not disproved by the intermediate comparison.
independent_verification.repair_check: Use logarithmic comparability or exponential inequalities retaining constants inside the exponent, and correct the near-zero limit labels.

findings.location: pp.27-28, proof of Theorem3.7 and equation(5.28)
findings.claim: The zero-measure branch takes the auxiliary parameter in the wrong direction; image-content labels are inconsistent with m>=n.
findings.proof: When L^n(E)=0, the bound contains [B^{-1}(r)]^n/r=Phi_B(1/r). Its vanishing follows as r->infinity, not r->0. For n=1,A(t)=4t^2 this coefficient is1/(2sqrt(r)), which diverges at0. The actual cube cover yields H^n_infinity(u(E))<=sum diam(u(Q_i))^n in R^m, not the printed L^n(u(E)) when m>n. Retain the content label throughout. For V=L^n(E)>0 choose r=kappa/(n^(n/2)V). The resulting bound is exactly2kappa^(n+1)||grad u||_A^n Phi_B(n^(n/2)V/kappa). For V=0 let r->infinity. Exhaustion and content continuity from below finish the asserted general-set bound.
findings.impact: Incorrect limiting direction and labels in a proof; the corrected cover argument proves the intended step without changing Theorem3.7.
findings.repair: Use r->infinity for zero volume and H^n_infinity for all target images in the proof. Zero-content cases of Theorem3.5 may invoke3.1(ii), covering phi=r^n as well.
findings.counterevidence: The positive-volume parameter calculation and its homogeneity are consistent with(3.18); no counterexample to that bound was obtained.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The relevant coefficient [B^{-1}(r)]^n/r=Phi_B(1/r) tends to zero as r tends to infinity. For n=1,A=4t^2 it is 1/(2 sqrt(r)) and diverges at zero. The diameter cover controls H_infinity^n(u(E)), including m>n, rather than the printed n-dimensional Lebesgue label.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The same cover estimate with r increasing gives the needed zero-volume conclusion. The positive-volume optimizing choice and exhaustion argument remain available; no false main theorem follows.
independent_verification.repair_check: Reverse the limiting direction, retain the image-content label and use the applicable theorem for the endpoint case.

findings.location: p.32 equations(6.12)-(6.15), with the use on pp.33-34
findings.claim: The printed Cantor cylinder mass exponent is inconsistent, and exact counts cannot start at j=1 for every permitted parameter.
findings.proof: With nu=1/2, the asserted #A_j=floor(2^{jnu}) and H^phi(Q cap M)<=c2^{-j} imply 0<H^phi(M)<=c2^{-j/2}->0, a contradiction. Page34 uses the required exponent2^{-jnu}. Separately, n=1,nu=3,j=1 requires8 dyadic intervals of length1/4 in[0,1], where only4 exist. Both parameters are allowed. A concrete repaired construction starts at sufficiently large j0, uses delta_j=2^{-2^j} and N_j=2^{floor(jnu)} comparable to2^{jnu}, and gives each parent N_(j+1)/N_j<=2^{ceil(nu)} separated children. Large j0 ensures room; initial cubes and enlarged supports may be placed inside(0,1)^n. Natural mass1/N_j per cylinder gives, for delta_(j+1)<=r<=delta_j, mu(B(x,r))<=C/N_j<=C'phi(r), since a ball meets only boundedly many dyadic j-cubes and adjacent gauge values have bounded ratio. Frostman/mass distribution yields positive H^phi(M); level covers give finite H^phi(M). Descendant covers of each j-cube give H^phi(Q cap M)<=C/N_j<=C2^{-jnu}. These are the exact estimates used later. The gradient exponent cancellation -nu/sigma+nu/n+(q-n+1)/n=0 remains valid. Bounded overlap supplies sum_Q|a_Q(x,y)|<=C sum_j j^{-delta}2^{-jnu/sigma}<infinity, meeting Lemma6.4's l1 assumption. The separation coefficient is bounded below by c j^{-delta}2^{-jnu/sigma}, retaining its fixed constant. Combining cylinder masses and kernels gives sum_j j^{delta sigma-mu}, convergent for1<delta<(mu-1)/sigma.
findings.impact: The incompatible p32 data cannot supply the admissible set and measure used in Theorem6.2. The p34 finite-energy proof needs cylinder factor2^(-jnu) to cancel kernel2^(jnu). This absent witness is a Major core construction failure. The explicit replacement verifies the required estimates; the corrected sharpness conclusion is not refuted.
findings.repair: Use2^{-jnu}, begin at sufficiently fine levels, and use asymptotic counts with bounded integer branching. State the l1 justification and retain fixed comparison constants.
findings.counterevidence: The theorem only needs asymptotic cardinality and bounded branching. The corrected construction preserves the exact exponents and works also for n=1,q>0.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The printed #A_j=floor(2^(j*nu)), finite positive H^phi(M) and cylinder mass <=c*2^(-j) are inconsistent for nu=1/2: summing masses tends to zero. For n=1,nu=3,j=1, eight distinct length-1/4 dyadic intervals cannot fit in [0,1]. Theorem 6.2's p.34 energy estimate actually needs cylinder mass of order 2^(-j*nu) to cancel its exponential kernel factor.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: A construction starting at large j0 with delta_j=2^(-2^j), N_j=2^floor(j*nu), bounded integer branching, separated cubes and mass 1/N_j gives Frostman bounds because adjacent gauge values have bounded ratio. It yields finite positive H^phi and the needed cylinder mass. Bounded overlap supplies the l1 coefficient condition, and the residual series sum j^(delta*sigma-mu) converges for 1<delta<(mu-1)/sigma.
independent_verification.repair_check: Replace the inconsistent data by the explicit admissible construction and mass bound. The printed proof lacks the required witness for its central sharpness result; a verified repair does not downgrade that failure. The sharpness conclusion itself is not refuted.

classification_reason: Major for the demonstrated gauge and Cantor-construction proof failures and their explicit core dependencies (F4/F7). Verified replacement arguments preserve the checked conclusions without lowering severity. F1-F3,F5,F6 remain Minor within their stated scopes; no principal-theorem counterexample is established.
rejected_candidates: The bars over E and E_j in pp.25-26 are visible on the actual images: these are compact closures, not claims that arbitrary E_j is compact.
The main theorem separately treats n=1 through B=A; the bad n' constant in Example3.6 does not invalidate that definition.
limitations: External Orlicz-Morrey inequality and general Hausdorff-content continuity were not fully independently reproved.
